newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutors close to cracking village arson.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutors close to cracking village arson.

text.p: A case against inhabitants of a small German village, accused of hiring skinheads to firebomb a planned hostel for foreigners in 1992, should soon be resolved, a state prosecutor said on Wednesday.
State prosecutor in the German town of Frankfurt on the Oder, Petra Marx said a suspect had made an extensive confession which had given more leads in the investigation.
The attack, one of a spate of racially-motivated attacks in the early 1990s, destroyed the hostel in Dolgenbrodt, north of Berlin, a day before 86 foreigners were to move in.
Nobody was injured but the fire caused 300,000 marks ($195,000) of damage.
Marx said an increasing number of clues pointed to other participants in the blaze.

A Berlin Tageszeitung newspaper report at the time of the fire said villagers, fearing crime would rise if the refugees came, collected cash as part of an offer of "financial and logistical support" for the attackers.

The village council condemned the attack at the time, but argued that the refugees did not belong in the community of some 250 people, whose main business is catering for visitors who keep weekend houses in the wooded region.
A man named as Silvio J. was found guilty last year of actually starting the fire for racist motives. He received a suspended sentence of two years.
Marx said a 23-year-old right-wing extremist detained on Tuesday had made the confession, which had provided new leads.
She said an arrest warrent had been issued for the man she named as Marco S., but said he had been released with a set of strict conditions for the period of the inquiry.
The man and his father are suspected of obtaining heating oil for the firebombs and also of constructing them.

Police are already investigating a 40-year-old flower dealer, named as Thomas O., who was arrested earlier this month and is accused of handing over 2,000 marks for the arson and then paying Silvio J. to keep quiet.
